$comment: Hand-edited (docs/SCHEMA.md). The Western Pacific's passenger trains and ferry in the Bay Area. Research: docs/research/sources-2c/western-pacific.md.

lines.name: Western Pacific trains, Oakland to Stockton
lines.summary: The Western Pacific's passenger trains from Oakland along Third St, by San Leandro, Hayward and Niles, through Niles Canyon to Pleasanton and Livermore and over the Altamont Pass toward Stockton and Salt Lake City: the Scenic Limited and the Feather River Express, from 1949 the California Zephyr.
lines.fate_note: The California Zephyr, the last train, left Oakland for Salt Lake City on its last trip on March 21, 1970 (AP). East of Fruitvale the line is the Union Pacific's Oakland Subdivision today, and ACE's trains run on it from Niles.

route.note: San Francisco passengers took the WP's own ferry from its mole (Tribune, 1910).
Back on its own mole after federal control (Tribune, 1920); still there on May 10, 1933 (WP timetable No. 20), and the move to Oakland Pier was still to come on June 9 (Point Richmond Progress).
Under federal control the WP's trains used the Southern Pacific's Oakland Pier: its own ferry station was out of use by October 25, 1918 (Tribune), and it withdrew in 1920 (Tribune).

At Oakland Pier again by October 1, 1933 (SP timetable No. 217) until the last ferry on the night of July 29, 1958; from July 30 the trains ended at Oakland, with buses to San Francisco (Independent-Journal).

sources.note: The first through train reached the depot at Third and Washington Sts at 4:15 p.m., August 22, 1910; the WP's ferry and mole.
The first eastbound overland, with ninety passengers, left Oakland at 5 p.m. on Monday, August 22, 1910; the first regular train from the east arrived on the 24th.
The union terminal still a proposal on May 28, 1918 (read in the scan's text only).
The California Zephyr "leaves for Salt Lake City on its last trip today", March 21, 1970: on or about March 1970.

lines.notes: Ends in March 1970: the last eastbound left Oakland on March 21 (AP, in a paper of that day), and the last westbound left Salt Lake City the same day, so reached Oakland about the 22nd, which no source read gives. The days the WP's trains moved to Oakland Pier in 1918 and in 1933, and back to its own mole in 1920, aren't sourced; the map shows each terminal only between dates a source has it in use. Drawn to the San Joaquin county line (decision 16). Not drawn: the WP's San José branch, Niles to East San José (1922 to July 1931, CRC Decisions 23837 and 24234).

lines.name: Western Pacific ferry, the WP mole to San Francisco
lines.summary: The Western Pacific's own ferry from its mole in Oakland to the Ferry Building, meeting its trains, except under federal control in 1918-20.
lines.fate_note: Given up in 1933, when the WP's trains moved to the Southern Pacific's Oakland Pier and its passengers to the SP's ferries, between June 9 and October 1, 1933 (Point Richmond Progress; SP timetable No. 217).

running.note: The WP mole is the trains' first station.
The move to Oakland Pier and the SP's ferries is still to come.

sources.note: The first regular train's San Francisco passengers took the boat, August 24, 1910.

Went into service "about Aug. 15" (1913), "taking the place of the stern-wheel steamer Telephone, which formerly connected the Western Pacific Railroad system at its terminal pier in Oakland and the ferry depot at the foot of Market street".

lines.notes: Its last day isn't sourced: drawn to June 9, 1933, the last date a source shows the WP still using its own mole (decision 20). The course is drawn over water between the terminals, not as steered.

photo.caption: The launch of the Western Pacific's ferry Edward T. Jeffery at the Moore & Scott yard in Oakland on July 19, 1913. From about August 15 she ran between the WP's pier in Oakland and the Ferry Building, in place of the stern-wheeler Telephone.
photo.author: International Marine Engineering

lines.name: Western Pacific trains, Niles to San José
lines.summary: The Western Pacific's branch trains from Niles by Irvington, Warm Springs, Milpitas and Berryessa to East San José, opened by a special from Oakland on August 23, 1922. By 1931, trains 101 and 102 ran between Niles and San José, meeting the Scenic Limited at Niles.
lines.fate_note: The Railroad Commission let the trains be replaced by a bus on June 29, 1931; the bus ran from July 13, 1931 and was itself given up under an order of November 16, 1931.

route.note: From Niles station the trains ran about half a kilometre along the main line to Niles Junction, which isn't drawn as part of this line.

sources.note: "riding from Oakland to San Jose on the first train over the new line".
Trains 101 and 102 between Niles and San José, connecting with the Scenic Limited; discontinued, with a bus substituted.
The bus ran from July 13, 1931; its abandonment authorized November 16, 1931.

lines.notes: The first train, on August 23, 1922, was the Oakland Chamber of Commerce's special; the first day of regular trains isn't sourced. The order replacing the trains is dated June 29, 1931, effective ten days later, and the bus began on July 13, 1931, so the last trains ran in July 1931; the day isn't stated.
